title: How to Do a Proper Squat at Home (For Beginners)
intro: The squat is the most basic leg and glute exercise you can do at home without equipment. Do it slowly with proper technique, and 2-3 times a week is enough to start.
muscles: Front thighs (quadriceps), glutes, back thighs (hamstrings) and core muscles. Honest note: squats strengthen your thighs, but they don't specifically remove thigh fat. Fat is reduced from your whole body through eating and daily movement.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
Take a breath and tighten your tummy a little, like you're about to cough.
Push your hips back, like you're about to sit on a chair.
Go down until your thighs are almost parallel to the floor, or as far as feels comfortable.
Make sure your knees follow the direction of your toes and your heels stay on the floor.
Push the floor with your whole foot to stand back up, while breathing out.
mistakes: Knees caving inward. Think 'push your knees out' in line with your toes.
Heels lifting up. This is usually a sign your weight is too far forward. Sit back a little more.
Going down too fast and 'bouncing' at the bottom. Take 2-3 seconds to go down and control every rep.
easier: Do squats to a chair: go down until your bum briefly touches the chair, then stand up. You can also hold a table or door for balance.
harder: Lower slowly for 3 seconds and hold for 2 seconds at the bottom (pause squat). Once your knees are comfortable, try split squats or jump squats.
dose: 2-3 sets x 8-12 reps. Rest 60-90 seconds between sets. Do it 2-3 times a week, every other day.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your knees, lower back or hips, not just tired muscles. If the pain persists or you have a history of knee injury, see a doctor or physiotherapist first.

faq.q: My knees make a 'crack' sound when I squat. Is it dangerous?
faq.a: Sounds without pain are usually normal and many people experience them. But if the sound comes with pain, swelling or your knee feels unstable, stop and see a physio.

faq.q: Can squatting every day slim down my thighs?
faq.a: Squats strengthen your thigh muscles, but you can't choose which fat comes off. Thigh fat reduces when your overall eating and daily movement are consistent. Squats help your body become stronger and more active.

Go as low as you can control without pain and without your heels lifting. For many beginners, thighs almost parallel to the floor is already okay. Your depth will improve naturally as you get used to it.
